objectives: Make the plural of nouns in the teacher's five plural groups, with her exceptions.
Count things with a number or många, and describe an amount with mycket.
Describe your home in a YKI-style interview answer and write a shopping message with quantities.

teacherNote.title: Listen for one and more than one
teacherNote.body: Elin invites Alex to dinner on Friday to celebrate Maja's maths test (Lecture 6). Mikko is Elin's partner (sambo) from Lecture 2. Before you listen, guess: will Alex bring one bottle of wine or two? Then listen for the plural endings. In Finland, ordinary wine is sold at Alko, the state alcohol shop; food shops may sell only drinks up to 8 % alcohol.

pages.title: Textbook page practice: Blommor och flaskor vin
pages.intro: This diary page belongs to the textbook's own story (Nora). Use it to notice group 1 plurals (-or) and time phrases such as för två veckor sedan and en vecka senare.

recallCues: Nora met a good-looking man two weeks ago. He wrote, they agreed to meet, and yesterday he sent her a flower.
The evening was perfect: delicious food, one bottle of wine, and talk about habits and favourite cakes.

sections.title: Meet the five plural groups
body: Plural means two or more. English usually adds -s: one car, two cars. Swedish has five plural endings, so your teacher sorts nouns into five plural groups.
Two clues point to the group. Is the noun an en-word or an ett-word? And what is its last letter? En blomma is an en-word that ends in -a, so it is group 1: två blommor.
These are the teacher's clues, not laws. They work for many nouns, and the teacher lists the exceptions you need now. Learn every new noun as a pair: en bil, två bilar.
To count, put the number before the plural. One is en or ett, so it matches the noun: en bil, ett äpple. From two upwards, use the plural: två bilar, tre äpplen.

Two mistakes cost the most. Do not give every noun the same ending, as English does with -s: två vänner and två hus, not två vännar or två husar. And do not drop the ending after a number: två bilar, not två bil.

rows: vecka → veckor, kvinna → kvinnor, penna → pennor
short everyday en-word; e as the last or second-last letter; ends in -ing
hund → hundar, pojke → pojkar, cykel → cyklar, klänning → klänningar
banan → bananer, tomat → tomater, frisör → frisörer, ingenjör → ingenjörer
äpple → äpplen, konto → konton, meddelande → meddelanden
ett-word ending in a consonant; en-word for a job or origin on -are
företag → företag, barn → barn, hus → hus, lärare → lärare

sections.memoryTip: Hindi and Marathi also change the end of a noun in the plural: लड़का → लड़के, मुलगा → मुलगे. Many Hindi and Marathi nouns keep the same form in the plural (Hindi एक घर, दो घर), just like Swedish group 5: ett hus, två hus. In Swedish only group 5 works like that, so two cars is två bilar, never två bil.
sections.tryIt: Say one and two aloud: blomma, bil, apelsin, möte, jobb.

activity.label: Five-group sort
activity.title: Which plural group is it?
activity.instructions: You see only the singular. Use en or ett and the last letter, choose the group, then say the plural aloud.

buckets.label: 2 · -ar
buckets.hint: short en-word; e near the end; -ing

buckets.label: 5 · no ending
buckets.hint: ett-word ending in a consonant; job on -are

items.why: Lampa is an en-word ending in -a: två lampor.
Stol is a short everyday en-word: två stolar.
Tidning ends in -ing: två tidningar.
Nyckel has e as its second-last letter. The e drops: två nycklar.
Tomat came into Swedish from another language: två tomater.
Servitör is a loanword, like frisör and direktör: två servitörer.
Äpple is an ett-word ending in a vowel: två äpplen.
Meddelande is an ett-word ending in a vowel: två meddelanden.
Hus is an ett-word ending in a consonant: två hus.
Läkare is a job ending in -are, so it has no plural ending: två läkare.

activity.summary: The clues work for many nouns. When you meet a new noun, check its plural in a dictionary and learn the pair.

sections.title: Groups 1 and 2: -or and -ar
body: Group 1: en-words that end in -a. Take away the -a and add -or: en blomma → blommor, en vecka → veckor, en kvinna → kvinnor, en flaska → flaskor.
Group 2 takes -ar. The teacher gives three clues. First, many short everyday en-words: en bil → bilar, en hund → hundar, en buss → bussar.

Second, en-words with e as the last or second-last letter. That e drops before -ar: en pojke → pojkar, en cykel → cyklar. Third, words that end in -ing: en tidning → tidningar, en klänning → klänningar.
The short-word clue is the weakest. Sak, katt, chef and vän look like group 2, but they take -er, and so does gäst (guest) from the dialogue. You meet them in the next topic.

examples.note: The e in -el drops: cyklar, not cykelar.

sections.memoryTip: Groups 1 and 2 both end in -r. Listen for the vowel before it: blomm-or, bil-ar.
sections.tryIt: Say the plural aloud: en penna, en buss, en tidning, en pojke.

activity.label: Spelling sort
activity.title: What happens to the word?
activity.instructions: Look at the singular and choose what happens in the plural. Then say both forms aloud.

items.why: Flaska ends in -a: två flaskor.
Soffa ends in -a: två soffor.
Nothing drops: två bussar.
Nothing drops: två julklappar, as on page 23.
Nothing drops: två dagar.
The final e drops: två superhjältar, as on page 23.
The e in -el drops: två gafflar.
The final e drops: två bullar.

activity.summary: Group 1: -a becomes -or. Group 2: add -ar, but first drop an e at the end or in -el.

sections.title: Group 3 and the teacher's exceptions
body: Group 3 takes -er. The teacher's clue: words that came into Swedish from other languages (loanwords). En banan → bananer, en tomat → tomater, en apelsin → apelsiner, and job words on -ör: en frisör → frisörer, en servitör → servitörer, en ingenjör → ingenjörer, en direktör → direktörer.

You cannot always know where a word comes from, so listen to it. Many group 3 loanwords are stressed on the last syllable: ba-NAN, to-MAT, apel-SIN, fri-SÖR, bil-JETT, tele-FON. Stress at the end is a strong hint for -er.
Two ett-words also take -er: ett museum → museer (take away -um first) and ett protein → proteiner. Ett vitamin → vitaminer on page 23 works the same way.

Four short en-words look like group 2 but take -er: en sak → saker, en katt → katter, en chef → chefer, en vän → vänner. En gäst → gäster from the dialogue works the same way. The ä in vän is short, so the n is written twice when an ending follows: vänner.
A few -er words also change their vowel: en bok → böcker, en son → söner (page 23). Learn these exceptions as whole pairs. Do not build a new rule from them.

examples.note: Stress on the last syllable: tele-FON → -er.
Chef means boss or manager, not a cook.
o becomes ö, like son → söner.

sections.memoryTip: One sentence holds the four short exceptions: Min chef har många saker, två katter och många vänner. (My manager has many things, two cats and many friends.)
sections.tryIt: Cover the plurals and say them: sak, katt, chef, vän, gäst, museum, protein, bok.

activity.label: -ar or -er?
activity.title: Short en-words: rule or exception?
activity.instructions: Every word here is a short en-word. Say the plural aloud first, then choose: does it follow the group 2 clue (-ar), or is it an exception or a loanword (-er)?

buckets.label: -er
buckets.hint: an exception, or a loanword stressed at the end

items.why: Dag follows the clue: två dagar.
The teacher's exception: två saker, never sakar.
Stol follows the clue: två stolar.
The teacher's exception: två katter.
Hund follows the clue: två hundar.
The teacher's exception: två vänner, with nn. The homework trap is vännar.
Buss follows the clue: två bussar, as on page 23.
Like sak and katt: två gäster, as in the dialogue.
The teacher's exception: två chefer.
A loanword stressed at the end, bil-JETT: två biljetter.

activity.summary: Most short en-words take -ar, but sak, katt, chef, vän and gäst take -er. Learn these as pairs.

sections.title: Groups 4 and 5: ett-words and jobs on -are
body: Group 4: ett-words that end in a vowel. Just add -n: ett möte → möten, ett äpple → äpplen, ett konto → konton, ett meddelande → meddelanden.
This -n is not the definite form from Lecture 5, where the ending means the: äpplet = the apple, but äpplen = apples; mötet = the meeting, but möten = meetings.

Group 5: ett-words that end in a consonant. Add nothing: ett jobb → två jobb, ett företag → två företag, ett barn → två barn, ett hus → två hus. The number or a word like många shows that it is plural.

Group 5 also has some en-words for jobs and origins. The teacher's examples end in -are: en lärare → två lärare, en läkare → två läkare, en italienare → två italienare. Here in Finland: en finländare → två finländare. Job words on -ör, like frisör, stay in group 3.

examples.note: An en-word, but a job on -are: no ending.
Ett datorspel, två datorspel: from the teacher's practice.

sections.memoryTip: Group 5 is like English sheep: one sheep, two sheep. Ett hus, två hus.
sections.tryIt: Count aloud in your room: ett bord, två bord … ett fönster, två fönster.

activity.label: Groups 4 and 5
activity.title: Add -n or add nothing?
activity.instructions: Look at en or ett and the last letter. Choose, then say singular and plural together.

buckets.label: add -n
buckets.hint: group 4: ett-word ending in a vowel

buckets.label: no ending
buckets.hint: group 5: ett-word ending in a consonant, or a job on -are

items.why: Konto ends in a vowel: två konton.
Yrke ends in a vowel: två yrken.
Ställe ends in a vowel: två ställen.
Spel ends in a consonant: två spel.
Bord ends in a consonant: två bord.
Glas ends in a consonant: två glas.
An origin word on -are: två italienare.
A job on -are: två lärare.

activity.summary: Ett-word + vowel: add -n. Ett-word + consonant, or a job or origin on -are: add nothing.

sections.title: Choose många or mycket
body: Use många (many) with plural things you count one by one: många bilar, många möten. Ask Hur många …? and answer with a number: Hur många bilar har ni? – Två.
Use mycket (much, a lot of) with an amount you do not count piece by piece: mycket vin, mycket kaffe, mycket tid. Ask Hur mycket …?
Pengar (money) is a plural word, but Swedish still says mycket pengar, because money is an amount. A container makes an amount countable: två flaskor vatten, tre koppar kaffe.

English a lot of fits both, and so do Hindi बहुत and Marathi खूप. Swedish makes you choose: a lot of cars is många bilar, never mycket bilar. The small words work the same way: några (some, a few) before plurals, lite (a little) before an amount: några tomater, lite mjölk.
Mycket also goes with verbs: Jag jobbar mycket (I work a lot). And inga means no before a plural: Jag har inga katter.

examples.en: I have many books at home.
How much coffee do you drink?
They want to earn a lot of money.

examples.fi: Köp några tomater och lite mjölk.
examples.en: Buy a few tomatoes and a little milk.

sections.memoryTip: If a number fits in front, use många: tre böcker → många böcker. If no number fits, as with pengar, tid or kaffe, use mycket. A lot of cars = många bilar.
sections.tryIt: Choose aloud: ___ äpplen; ___ kaffe; ___ möten; ___ pengar.

activity.label: Ask Elin
activity.title: Ask Elin about Friday's dinner
activity.instructions: Each fact is hidden. Choose the question that would really get it: många or mycket, the right plural ending, and the verb straight after the question words. Elin answers aloud.

reply.en: There will be four of us.

gaps.why: You count guests, so hur många. Gäst takes -er, like sak and katt: gäster.

reply.fi: Inte så mycket. En flaska räcker.
reply.en: Not that much. One bottle is enough.

gaps.why: Wine is an amount, so hur mycket. The verb dricker comes straight after the question words.

reply.fi: Sex äpplen. Jag bakar en äppelkaka.
reply.en: Six apples. I am baking an apple cake.

gaps.why: Ett äpple is group 4: add -n, äpplen. Äpplet means the apple (the definite form from Lecture 5).
Stol is a short en-word: stolar. The -or ending is for en-words on -a, like lampa → lampor.

reply.en: Yes, we have lots of glasses.

gaps.why: Ett glas is group 5: no ending. A yes/no question starts with the verb (Lecture 2): Har ni …?

activity.summary: Hur många + a plural you can count; hur mycket + an amount. In a question the verb comes second, right after hur många or hur mycket.

sections.title: Meet, see and play: verb pairs
body: Träffar means meet someone. A person comes after it (the object): Jag träffar Elin i kväll. Träffas means meet each other, so no person comes after it: Vi träffas i kväll. In the past: träffade and träffades.
Ser and ses work the same way: Vi ser en älg (we see a moose). Vi ses! means See you! (we will see each other).
Swedish has two verbs for play. Leker is play for children and pets: Barnen leker i trädgården. Spelar is for games, sports and instruments: Jag spelar fotboll. Alex spelar datorspel.
Lagar means repair: Han lagar cyklar. Laga mat means cook: Vi lagar mat tillsammans.

examples.fi: Vi träffades för två veckor sedan.
examples.note: The past of träffas; för … sedan is on page 22.

examples.en: Two children are playing in the garden.
I play football and computer games.

sections.memoryTip: Here the -s in träffas and ses means each other: vi träffas, vi ses.
sections.tryIt: Say two true sentences: Jag träffar … i kväll. · Jag spelar …

activity.label: Which verb?
activity.title: Match each situation to its Swedish verb
activity.instructions: Read what is happening and choose the verb that fits. Then say a short sentence with it.
activity.pattern: Träffar and ser need a person or thing after them; träffas and ses mean each other. Children leker; games, sports and instruments take spelar.

guided.prompt: Write the plural: en pojke → två ___.
answers: pojkar

assignment.title: Episode 7 mission: Things at home
assignment.instructions:
CORE: Answer the YKI-style interview theme Berätta om ditt hem (Tell about your home) in five or six sentences. Use at least three plural groups, one exact number, många, mycket and inga, and link two ideas with men or för.

WRITING: Answer a friend at the shop with a short shopping message (30–55 words).

RETURN: Tomorrow, name five things at home from memory and give their plurals.
assignment.model: Hemma har jag två lampor, fyra stolar, många böcker, fem blommor och två cyklar.

takeaways: Group 1 (-or): en-words ending in -a, en blomma → blommor. Group 2 (-ar): many short en-words, and words with e near the end or -ing, en pojke → pojkar.

Group 3 (-er): words from other languages, often stressed on the last syllable (bananer, telefoner), plus the exceptions saker, katter, chefer, vänner, gäster, museer, proteiner. Group 4 (-n): ett-words ending in a vowel; äpplen = apples, but äpplet = the apple. Group 5 (no ending): ett-words ending in a consonant, and jobs on -are.

Count with många and några; describe an amount with mycket and lite. Avoid the three big mistakes: två bil, två vännar, mycket bilar. You träffar someone, but vi träffas; children leker, and you spelar games.

pronunciation.text: En blomma, två blommor. En bil, två bilar. En banan, två bananer. Ett museum, två museer. Ett möte, två möten. En vän, två vänner.
pronunciation.tip: The stress stays on the same syllable as in the singular: BI-lar, ba-NA-ner, mu-SE-er (say both e's). Say the unstressed ending clearly, because it is the only sign of the group. Finland-Swedish weakens endings less than the Sweden-Swedish voices do, and it has no two-step word melody (accent 2) on words like bilar and blommor, so you do not need to copy that melody. Keep the ä short in vän and vänner.

listening.text: Elin och Mikko bor i en lägenhet med tre rum. I vardagsrummet har de en soffa, fyra stolar och många böcker. På bordet står två lampor och tre glas. De har också fem blommor men inga katter. I köket finns många tallrikar, några flaskor vatten och sex äpplen. Elin dricker mycket kaffe, så hon har många koppar. Två dagar i veckan jobbar hon hemma. Då har hon många videomöten. Hon tycker om museer och har två biljetter till Ateneum på söndag.

listening.explanation: De har också fem blommor men inga katter. Inga means no, before a plural.

speaking.prompt: YKI-style interview theme: Berätta om ditt hem (Tell about your home). Give the interviewer five or six sentences: your rooms, things you have many of, one thing you do not have much of, and one thing you have none of. Use at least three plural groups and link two ideas with men or för.
speaking.help: Hemma har jag … · I rummet finns … · Jag har många … · Jag har inte så mycket … · Jag har inga … · …, men … · …, för …
speaking.model: Jag bor i en liten lägenhet med ett rum och ett kök. I rummet finns en soffa, två lampor och många böcker. I köket har jag fyra stolar och många glas, men inte så mycket kaffe. Jag har också två cyklar. Jag har fem blommor, men inga katter.

writing.prompt: Write a short shopping message to a friend. Use plural nouns and quantities.
writing.situation: A YKI-style message. Two friends are coming to your place for dinner tonight. Your friend Sanna is at the S-market and texts you: “Jag är i butiken. Behöver du något?” (I am at the shop. Do you need anything?) Write back. As in the test, start and end the message in a suitable way and cover every point.
points: Ask for at least three things, each with a number or några.
Use at least two different plural groups (for example -or and -er).
Say one thing you do not need, with mycket or många (Jag har mycket …).
Say how many you will be tonight, and end the message.
writing.help: Hej Sanna! · Tack, vad snällt! · Kan du köpa …? · två flaskor … · sex äpplen · några tomater · Köp inte …, för jag har mycket … · Vi blir … i kväll. · Vi ses!
writing.model: Hej Sanna! Tack, vad snällt! Kan du köpa två flaskor vatten, sex äpplen och några tomater? Köp inte kaffe, för jag har mycket kaffe hemma. Jag har också många glas. Vi blir tre i kväll. Vi ses snart! / Alex
